notes.body: Capture file where changes were tested.[zvt_sale.pcapng](/uploads/8ddeedfe3e30d84f2998b8146f743463/zvt_sale.pcapng)

There is functions to do this allready, the simplest from packet-nas_eps.c 
 proto_tree_add_item(tree, hf_nas_eps_emm_imei, tvb, curr_offset, len, ENC_BCD_DIGITS_0_9 | ENC_BCD_SKIP_FIRST);
If you look at the history you can probably see different aproaches to do this. See also tvb_bcd_dig_to_wmem_packet_str().

I know it, I have seen https://ask.wireshark.org/question/1138/dissector-plugin-binary-coded-decimal-encoding/ But I can't use this approach because it changes order of digits. It there is a byte 0x12 it is converted to string "21". Therefore ENC_BCD_DIGITS_0_9 is not suitable for ZVT. tvb_bcd_dig_to_wmem_packet_str() is no help because it is exactly the function which is called when you use ENC_BCD_DIGITS_0_9. This behavior is mentioned here: https://seclists.org/wireshark/2013/Dec/205 I  wrote my BCD function because I have searched Wireshark code and couldn't find normal BCD decoding function, just this 3GPP-style.

@AndersBroman can we enhance/replace the BCD functions we have now so that we can pass an 'endianness' to it, specifying the order in which the BCD digits in a byte are consumed? The existing functions would then be mapped to the LE versions of it.

Hi,
Yes I was thinking about something along those lines.
Regards
Anders
Should I add the new function in this merge request or create a new one?
If it affects a lot off existing files it may be better as a separate one?

Is the BCD refactoring OK?
Meanwhile I have fixed Registration packet dissection. The code assumed that service byte always followes CC. That's not true. The specification says the opposite: "If <service-byte> is sent, <CC> must also be present." Service byte is optional. The code treated it as mandatory and when it was absent it didn't parse CC nor TLV.
